ComplexHeatmap Plot Orchestrator

Source: R/complexheatmap_plot_orchestrator.R
ComplexHeatmapPlotOrchestrator.Rd

Reads a 'ComplexHeatmap' heat map – a Heatmap, or a HeatmapList holding one or more – as one subplot per heat map, each holding one heat layer (ComplexHeatmapLayerProcessor). Experimental.

The object is drawn once, with ComplexHeatmap::draw(), and the drawing is grabbed as a grid tree (complexheatmap_capture()). The SVG is that tree, and the layer is read from the HeatmapList that same draw returned, so the order of the rows and columns read is the order drawn even where drawing decides it afresh – row_km's k-means, say, which an undrawn Heatmap runs again on every draw. Pass what draw() returned to read the very chart that was shown.

Lists. A list of several heat maps (ht1 + ht2, ht1 %v% ht2) is read heat map by heat map, each from its own matrix, labels and drawn order – which the drawing shares across the list, the rows of a horizontal list and the columns of a vertical one – into a subplot of its own. A horizontal list is one row of subplots, left to right; a vertical list one column of them, its rows written bottom first, as pheatmap's grid is (PheatmapPlotOrchestrator): a heat layer's selectors are a grid, which maidr.js does not measure a subplot by, so it orders the subplots as written, where Up moves to the next row. Each heat map's title is its own column title, and the chart's the one draw() was given for the whole list.

Only the matrices are read. The dendrograms set the order the cells are read in but are not read themselves, and neither are annotations, between heat maps or around them, or legends. A heat map whose matrix is not numeric (a discrete heat map of categories) is left out of a list that holds a numeric one, with a message (class maidr_complexheatmap_skipped) naming it; a chart with no numeric heat map falls back to an image.

Whether that size was asked for, by default when either side is given; see chart_canvas_size()

ComplexHeatmapPlotOrchestrator$extract_layout()

Read the chart's title and its rows' title

The title is the column title draw() was given for the whole list, else, for a single heat map, its own column title when it is one string; the rows' title likewise from the row titles. A title per slice of a split names no axis and is not read.

Usage

ComplexHeatmapPlotOrchestrator$extract_layout()

Returns

List with title and row_title

ComplexHeatmapPlotOrchestrator$heatmap_layout()

The title and rows' title of one heat map of a list

Its own column title, and the rows' title draw() was given, else its own row title, else, in a horizontal list, whose rows are shared, the main heat map's: the one row title 'ComplexHeatmap' draws for them.
